landing.hero_sub: We leverage data analytics and offline technology to bring expert medical intelligence directly to rural health workers, ensuring verified facts and sustainable public health.
landing.mission_quote: HealthGuard Uganda exists to bridge the information gap in rural healthcare. By combining accessible fact-checking with complex epidemiological data analytics, we help health workers identify outbreaks early, optimize care, and verify claims instantly.
landing.feature_factcheck_desc: Instant verification of health rumors against official Ministry of Health guidelines, available fully offline.
landing.feature_data_desc: Real-time tracking of localized health trends and symptom outbreaks across entire rural regions.
landing.feature_expert_desc: Connecting rural health workers directly with certified medical experts in seconds for complex triage.
landing.impact_sub: Empowering communities and strengthening healthcare delivery through evidence-based technology.
landing.stat_misinfo_desc: Significant decrease in community health rumors and false medical claims in our active districts.
landing.stat_hw_desc: Equipped with offline-capable diagnostic and fact-checking toolkits for prompt field interventions.
landing.stat_response_desc: Fast verification of emergent health queries mapped to official guidelines.
landing.stat_clinics_desc: Providing reliable digital infrastructure and local database access in remote rural areas.
landing.partners_sub: Working hand-in-hand with leading health institutions to build resilient public health systems.
landing.footer_desc: Protecting livelihoods by verifying health facts. We are committed to sustainable public health and empowering communities through accurate information.

malaria-2026-05.title: Malaria Surge — Northern Uganda
malaria-2026-05.description: A seasonal rise in Plasmodium falciparum cases has been recorded across Gulu, Lira, and Kitgum districts following heavier-than-expected May rains. Health facilities report a 34% increase in confirmed RDT-positive cases compared to April. MoH urges sleeping under LLINs and seeking treatment within 24 hours of fever onset.

cholera-2026-05.title: Cholera Outbreak — Kasese District
cholera-2026-05.description: The Uganda Virus Research Institute (UVRI) has confirmed a cholera (Vibrio cholerae O1) cluster linked to contaminated water sources near the Rwenzori foothills. 47 cases and 2 deaths have been reported. ORS centres are operational at Kasese General Hospital. Residents are advised to boil or treat all drinking water.

mpox-2026-04.title: Mpox (Monkeypox) — Nakaseke & Luweero
mpox-2026-04.description: MoH has confirmed 12 laboratory-verified Mpox Clade Ib cases in Nakaseke and Luweero districts, connected to cross-border movement from the DRC. Contact tracing teams are deployed. Vaccination with JYNNEOS is ongoing for high-risk contacts. Public is advised to avoid contact with sick animals and report rash-like symptoms.

measles-2026-03.title: Measles Alert — Karamoja Sub-Region
measles-2026-03.description: Low vaccination coverage (estimated 52%) in Moroto, Nakapiripirit, and Amudat districts has resulted in a measles resurgence. 89 suspected cases with 6 confirmed deaths — predominantly children under 5. UNEPI reactive vaccination campaigns are scheduled. Caregivers are urged to present children at the nearest health facility.

typhoid-2026-03.title: Typhoid Fever Cluster — Kampala Slums
typhoid-2026-03.description: A cluster of Salmonella typhi infections has been linked to contaminated food vendors in Bwaise, Kamwokya, and Katanga. 23 confirmed cases, mostly young adults aged 15–30. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing shows 60% resistance to ciprofloxacin. MoH advises eating only properly cooked food and washing hands frequently.

rabies-2026-02.title: Rabies Deaths — Lyantonde & Rakai Districts
rabies-2026-02.description: Three human deaths from rabies have been confirmed following dog bites in Lyantonde and Rakai districts. Investigations indicate low dog vaccination coverage in affected sub-counties. MoH is conducting mass dog vaccination campaigns. Anyone bitten by an animal should immediately wash the wound and seek PEP at a health facility.

covid-2026-01.title: COVID-19 XEC Variant — Minor Wave
covid-2026-01.description: A minor uptick in SARS-CoV-2 cases attributed to the XEC sub-variant has been detected in Kampala and Wakiso. 340 confirmed cases in January 2026 — no significant hospitalizations. Genomic surveillance by UVRI is ongoing. Vulnerable individuals (elderly, immunocompromised) are encouraged to get updated XBB booster doses.

tb-2026-jan.title: Tuberculosis — Annual MoH Report
tb-2026-jan.description: Uganda notified 84,000 TB cases in 2025, an increase of 8% from 2024. Drug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) accounts for 3.4% of new cases. Co-infection with HIV remains high at 39%. MoH emphasizes completing the full 6-month treatment course. TB care is free at all government health facilities.
